name: Schrödinger Anderson localisation 1
description: Linear Schrödinger equation: two identical packets start at rest. The bottom one spreads into clear space and keeps spreading until the border absorbs it. The top one sits in a random potential: the waves it sends out scatter back off the disorder and interfere so as to cancel the outward flow, and it stops spreading, held in place with no walls around it. This is Anderson localisation (Nobel 1977), why disorder can turn a metal into an insulator. A wall separates the halves. Try: Restart a few times (the disorder changes each time).
